newsitem.title: UK: ING Barings talks options with Dillon Read.
newsitem.headline: ING Barings talks options with Dillon Read.

text.p: ING Barings, the investment banking arm of Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV, said on Thursday it was talking to U.S. investment bank Dillon Read & Co about the future of the relationship between them.

An ING Barings spokesman told Reuters that Dillon Read's option to buy back ING's 25 percent stake in the firm expired at the end of June and that "talks are going on between Dillon Read and ING Barings as to how to proceed from there".

Earlier, London's Evening Standard newspaper reported that ING Barings, which was formed when the Dutch financial services giant rescued British bank Barings in 1995, would pay between $425 and $450 million for the remaining 75 percent of Dillon Read.

Banking sources said talks had been going on in both London and New York between Marinus Minderhoud, ING group's chairman of corporate and investment banking management, and Dillon Read chairman John Birklund. They said ING chief executive Aad Jacobs was also likely to have been involved in the talks.

Dillon Read partners are believed to have the right to buy the 25 percent stake back at book value, banking sources said. But with ING Barings keen to beef up its presence on Wall Street, Dillon Read may be persuaded to opt for a takeover.
The New York-based firm has a good presence in mergers and acquisitions for mid-market companies and this has helped ING Barings' own corporate finance operation in London, bankers said.
ING Barings already employs around 1,200 people in New York, specialising in global high yield businesses, emerging markets and banking. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
